title: Geobacter metallireducens gen. nov. sp. nov., a microorganism capable of coupling the complete oxidation of organic compounds to the reduction of iron and other metals
authors: D. R. Lovley; S. J. Giovannoni; D. C. White; J. E. Champine; E. J. P. Phillips; Y. A. Gorby; S. Goodwin
doi_resolution: Direct DOI fetch unavailable; DOI/title corroborated by USGS search metadata. Actual author-hosted primary scan inspected.
conditional_excerpts: For growth with Fe(III)-citrate (50 mM) or nitrate (5-20 mM)
the CaCl2 · 2H2O and the Fe(III) oxide were omitted.
locator: Printed page 337, left column, Source of organism and culturing procedures
transcription: Short separate excerpts from the same sentence; subscripts flattened and line breaks normalized. Not spliced into one quote.

remaining: The 1988b methods, its 1984 stock cross-reference and Balch 1979 Table 1 have now been visually inspected; see source-chain.md. Establish which stock version and dose applies to each target before mutation.
Resolve the supplied acetate chemical form before accepting the database molarity derived from a mass amount.
Check iron-atom versus oxide-formula-unit basis rather than assuming they are interchangeable.
Table 2 on page 339 has now been inspected. Map its donor conditions and read every target ingredient before approving a cohort mutation.
Do not transfer cell-suspension cytochrome-assay concentrations or non-utilized conditions into positive growth assertions.
